pp:me:2007:q7.title: GATE ME 2007 | Set 1 | Question: 7
pp:me:2007:q7.question: Consider an incompressible laminar boundary layer flow over a flat plate of length L, aligned with the direction of an oncoming uniform free stream. If F is the ratio of the drag force on the front half of the plate to the drag force on the rear half, then

primary.subtopicLabel: Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics - Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory
detailed_solution.markdown:
Drag force,

$$\begin{aligned} F_{D} &=C_{f} \times \frac{1}{2} \rho A V^{2}=\frac{1.328}{\sqrt{\text{Re}_{L}}} \times \frac{1}{2} \rho A V^{2} \\ &=\frac{1.328}{\sqrt{\frac{\rho L V}{\mu}}} \times \frac{1}{2} \rho \times A \times L \times V^{2}\\ \text{i.e. }F_{D} &\propto \sqrt{L} \\ \end{aligned}$$

Now Drag force on front half,

$$\begin{aligned} \quad F_{D R} &\propto \sqrt{\frac{L}{2}} \\ \therefore F_{D / 2}&=\frac{F_{D}}{\sqrt{2}} \end{aligned}$$

Drag force on rear half,

$$\begin{aligned} F_{D / 2}^{\prime}&=F_{D}-F_{D / 2}=\left(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) F_{D}\\ \text{Now} F&=\frac{F_{D / 2}}{F_{D / 2}^{\prime}}=\frac{\frac{F_{D}}{\sqrt{2}}}{\left(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) F_{D}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}>1\\ \therefore \quad F&>1 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:me:2007:q36.title: GATE ME 2007 | Set 1 | Question: 36
pp:me:2007:q36.question: Atmospheric air at a flow rate of 3 kg/s (on dry basis) enters a cooling and dehumidifying coil with an enthalpy of   85 kJ/kg of dry air and a humidity ratio of 19 grams/kg of dry air. The air leaves the coil with an enthalpy of 43 kJ/kg of dry air and a humidity ratio of 8 grams/kg of dry air. If the condensate water leaves the coil with an enthalpy of 67 kJ/kg, the required cooling capacity of the coil in kW is

detailed_solution.markdown: Given data: Mass flow rate of dry air $$\begin{aligned} m_{a}&=3 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ h_{1}&=85 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \text { of dry air } \\ \omega_{1}&=19 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{kg} \text { of dry air } \\ &=0.019 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{kg} \text { of dry air } \\ h_{2}&=43 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \text { of dry air } \\ \omega_{2}&=8 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{kg} \text { of dry air } \\ &=0.008 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{kg} \text { of dry air } \end{aligned}$$ Enthalpy of condenrate water leaves the cooling $$\begin{aligned} \text { coil: } h_{f g}&=67 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ \omega_{1}&=\frac{m_{v 1}}{m_{a}}\\ \text{or }\quad m_{v 1}&=\omega_{1} m_{a}=0.019 \times 3 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ & =0.057 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s}, \text{mass of water vapour at inlet} \\ \end{aligned}$$ Similarly, $m_{v 2}=\omega_{2} m_{a}=0.008 \times 3$ $=0.024 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s},$ mass of water vapour at outlet Mass flow rate of condensate, $$\begin{aligned} m_{w} &=m_{v 1}+m_{v 2} \\ &=0.057+0.024=0.033 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$ Cooling capacity of the coil, $$\begin{aligned} Q&=m\left(h_{1}-h_{2}\right)-m_{w} h_{f g}\\ \text{where }m\left(h_{1}-h_{2}\right)&= \text{sensible heat removed}\\ \therefore m_{w} h_{f g}&= \text{ Latent heat removed}\\ Q &=3(85-43)-0.033 \times 67 \\ &=123.79 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}$$ Alternatively Mass flow rate of condensate, $$\begin{aligned} m_{w} &=m_{a}\left(\omega_{1}-\omega_{2}\right) \\ &=3 \times(0.019-0.008) \\ &=0.033 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$ Applying energy balance equation, we get $$\begin{aligned} m_{a} h_{1} &=m_{a} h_{2}+m_{w} h_{f g}+Q \\ 3 \times 85 &=3 \times 43+0.033 \times 67+Q \\ Q &=123.8 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:me:2007:q37.title: GATE ME 2007 | Set 1 | Question: 37

pp:me:2007:q40.title: GATE ME 2007 | Set 1 | Question: 40
pp:me:2007:q40.question:
Which combination of the following statements about steady incompressible forced vortex flow is correct?
P: Shear stress is zero at all points in the flow.
Q: Vorticity is zero at all points in the flow.
R: Velocity is directly proportional to the radius from the centre of the vortex.
S: Total mechanical energy per unit mass is constant in the entire flow field.

detailed_solution.markdown: Given: The flow is a steady incompressible forced vortex flow. Key property of forced vortex: $v = \omega r$ Evaluation of statements: P: Shear stress is zero at all points in the flow. In a forced vortex, the fluid rotates like a rigid body. There is no relative motion between adjacent fluid layers, hence no velocity gradient in the radial direction. $\therefore \text{Shear stress} = 0$ Statement P is TRUE. Q: Vorticity is zero at all points in the flow. For a forced vortex, vorticity is given by $\text{Vorticity} = 2\omega$ which is constant and non-zero. Statement Q is FALSE. R: Velocity is directly proportional to the radius from the centre of the vortex. From the forced vortex relation, $v = \omega r$ Velocity increases linearly with radius. Statement R is TRUE. S: Total mechanical energy per unit mass is constant in the entire flow field. In a forced vortex, pressure and kinetic energy vary with radius, so total mechanical energy is not constant throughout the flow field (it is constant only along a streamline). Statement S is FALSE. Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

$\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2} x}{\mathrm{d} t^{2}}+2\zeta \omega _{n}\frac{\mathrm{d} x}{\mathrm{d} t}+\omega _{n}^{2}x=0$

$\frac{\mathrm{d} ^2x}{\mathrm{d} t^2}+2\zeta \omega_n\frac{\mathrm{d} x}{\mathrm{d} t}+\omega_n^2 x=0$

$\ddot x+2\zeta \omega_n\dot x+\omega_n^2 x=0$

Logarithmic decrement is given by

$\frac{X}{x_{n+1}} =e^{\frac{2\pi n\zeta}{\sqrt{1-\zeta^2}}}$

$x_{n+1} =Xe^{-\frac{2\pi n\zeta}{\sqrt{1-\zeta^2}}}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

primary.subtopicLabel: Static Dynamic Loading and Failure Theories

detailed_solution.concept: Machine Design - Static Dynamic Loading and Failure Theories
detailed_solution.markdown:
Assuming guided end to be fixed and other end given as hinged. The crippling load according to euler's equation,

$$\begin{aligned} P_{c r} &=\frac{2 \pi^{2} E I}{L^{2}} \\ I &=\frac{\pi}{64}(20)^{4}=7853.9 \mathrm{mm}^{4} \\ E &=200 \times 10^{9} \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m}^{2}=200 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{mm}^{2} \\ &=\frac{2 \pi^{2} \times 200 \times 10^{3} \times 7853.9}{(700)^{2}}=63.27 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$$

Factor of safety

$=\frac{\text { Crippling load }}{\text { Working load }}=\frac{63.27}{10}=6.32$

$I=a L+b$

where a and b are constant

Solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$$\begin{aligned} a&=-20 \\ \text{and }b&=600 \end{aligned}$$

Then arc characteristic equation

$I=-20 L+600 \qquad(a)$

from equation (a) and (b)

$$\begin{aligned} E &=80-\frac{80}{800}(-20 L+600) \\ &=80-0.1(-20 L+600) \\ &=80+2 L-60 \\ &=20+2 L \end{aligned}$$

If the specific heats of the working fluid are constant and the value of specific heat ratio $\gamma$ is 1.4, the thermal efficiency (%) of the cycle is

detailed_solution.markdown: the The given cycle is Lenoir cycle for which efficiency is given by $$\begin{aligned} \eta&=1-\frac{\gamma\left(r_{p}^{1 / \gamma}-1\right)}{r_{p}-1}\\ \text{where }\quad \gamma&=1.4 \\ r_{p} &=\frac{p_{3}}{p_{2}}=\frac{400}{100}=4 \\ \therefore \quad \eta &=1-\frac{1.4\left(\frac{4 \sqrt{1.4}}{4-1}\right)}{4-1} \\ &=21.05 \% \end{aligned}$$ Alternatively Process 2-3 $$\begin{aligned} Q_{23} &=\left(U_{3}-U_{2}\right)+W_{2-3} \\ Q_{23} &=\left(U_{3}-U_{2}\right)+0 \\ &=m_{v}\left(T_{3}-T_{2}\right) \\ &=m_{v}\left(\frac{p_{3} V_{3}}{m R}-\frac{p_{2} V_{2}}{m R}\right) \\ &=\frac{c_{v}}{R}\left(p_{3} v_{3}-p_{2} V_{2}\right) \\ &=\frac{c_{v}}{c_{p}-c_{v}}(400 \times 1-100 \times 1) \\ Q_{23} &=\frac{1}{\gamma-1}(400-100) \\ &=\frac{300}{1.4-1}=\frac{300}{0.4}=750 \mathrm{kJ} \\ Q_{1-2} = & \left(U_{2}-U_{1}\right)+W_{1-2} \\ & =m_{0}\left(T_{2}-T_{1}\right)+p\left(V_{2}-V_{1}\right) \\ & =m_{0}\left[\frac{p_{2} V_{2}}{m R}-\frac{p_{1} V_{1}}{m R}\right]+p\left(V_{2}-V_{1}\right)\\ &=\frac{c_{v}}{R}\left[p\left(V_{2}-V_{1}\right)\right]+p\left(V_{2}-V_{1}\right) \\ &=p\left(V_{2}-v_{1}\right)\left\{\frac{c_{v}}{R}+1\right\} \\ &\qquad \because V_{2}=1 \mathrm{m}^{3}\\ &=p\left(1-v_{1}\right)\left\{\frac{c_{v}}{c_{p}-c_{v}}+1\right\} \\ &=100\left(1-V_{1}\right)\left\{\frac{1}{\gamma-1}+1\right\} \end{aligned}$$ Calculating $V_{1}$ $$\begin{aligned} P_{3} V_{3}^{\gamma} &=P_{1} V_{1}^{\gamma} \\ \therefore \quad V_{1} &=\left[\frac{P_{3} \cdot V_{3}^{\gamma}}{P_{1}}\right]^{\frac{1}{\gamma}} \\ &=\left[\frac{400}{100} \times 1\right]^{\frac{1}{1.4}}=2.692 \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ Q_{1-2} &\left.=100[1-2.692] \times\left\{\frac{1}{0.4}+1\right\}\right\} \\ &=-592.2 \mathrm{kJ} \end{aligned}$$ (minus sign represent heat is rejected) There is no heat transfer in process 3-1 as it is reversible adiabatic process. Efficiency of cycle, $$\begin{aligned} \eta &=1-\frac{Q_{\text {reject }}}{Q_{\text {added }}}=1-\frac{592.2}{750} \\ &=0.2104=21.04 \% \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{p_{A}}{p_{g}}+\frac{u_{0}^{2}}{2 g}+z_{A}&=\frac{p_{A}}{p g}+\frac{V_{m}^{2}}{2 g}+z_{B} \\ \frac{p_{A}}{\rho g}+\frac{u_{0}^{2}}{2 g}&=\frac{p_{B}}{\rho g}+\frac{V_{m}^{2}}{2 g} \quad \because z_{A}=z_{B}\\ \text{or }\quad \frac{p_{A}}{\rho g}-\frac{p_{B}}{\rho g}&=\frac{V_{m}^{2}}{2 g}-\frac{u_{0}^{2}}{2 g} \\ \text{or }\quad p_{A}-p_{B}&=\frac{\rho V_{m}^{2}}{2}-\frac{\rho u_{0}^{2}}{2} \\ \text{Now, the ratio}\\ \frac{p_{A}-p_{B}}{\frac{1}{2} \rho u_{0}^{2}} &=\frac{\frac{\rho V_{m}^{2}}{2}-\frac{\rho u_{0}^{2}}{2}}{\frac{1}{2} \rho u_{0}^{2}} \\ &=\frac{V_{m}^{2}-u_{0}^{2}}{u_{0}^{2}}=\left(\frac{V_{m}}{u_{0}}\right)^{2}-1 \end{aligned}$$

Substituting the value of $\frac{V_{m}}{u_{0}}=\frac{1}{1-(\delta / H)}$

$\frac{p_{A}-p_{B}}{\frac{1}{2} \rho u_{0}^{2}}=\frac{1}{[1-(\delta / H)]^{2}}-1$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:me:2007:q84.title: GATE ME 2007 | Set 1 | Question: 84
pp:me:2007:q84.question:
A low carbon steel bar of 147 mm diameter with a length of 630 mm is being turned with uncoated carbide insert. The observed tool lives are 24 min and 12 min for cutting velocities of 90 m/min and 120 m/min respectively. The feed and depth of cut are 0.2 mm/rev and 2 mm respectively. Use the unmachined diameter to calculate the cutting velocity.

When tool life is 20 min, the cutting velocity in m/min is

detailed_solution.concept: Manufacturing Engineering - Machining and Machine Tool Operation
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given, $T_1=24 min, T_2 =12 min, V_1=90m/min, V_2=120m/min$

We have to calculate velocity, when tool life is 20 minute.

First of all we calculate the values of n, From the Taylor's tool life equation,

$VT^n=C$

For case 1st and 2nd, we can write,

$$\begin{aligned} V_1T_1^n &= V_2T_2^n\\ \left ( \frac{T_1}{T_2} \right )^n &= \frac{V_2}{V_1} \\ \left ( \frac{24}{12} \right )^n &=\frac{120}{90} \\ 2^n&= 1.33\\ n \log 2&=\log 1.33 \\ n \times 0.301 &=0.124 \\ n&= 0.412 \end{aligned}$$

For $V_3$, we can write from tool life equation,

$$\begin{aligned} V_1T_1^n &= V_3T_3^n\\ 90 \times (24)^{0.412}&=V_3(20)^{0.412}\\ 333.34 &=V_3 \times 3.435\\ V_3 &=97\; m/min \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.
